headline: Starting snapshot from the November 2026 research. Add an Anthropic API key in Settings to refresh it daily.

valuation.summary: News puts the Shiller CAPE above 40, its highest since 2000, and US stock value above 2.5 times GDP; the data agrees (CAPE and stock value / GDP both near records). Goldman Sachs sees no valuation bubble inside tech, which fits the benchmark readings.

items.text: The Shiller CAPE reached 41.2 in August, its highest since September 2000.
Dean Baker's AI Bubble Monitor: market P/E 39.6 against 43.8 in 2000; US stock value more than 2.5 times GDP.
Goldman Sachs sees no valuation bubble in technology; the risk is an earnings bubble.

expansion.summary: Prices have outrun industrial output but real earnings have kept pace, the split Goldman describes as a possible earnings bubble. The explosive-root test fires on real price only.

items.text: Goldman: earnings, not multiples, drove tech gains; implied 10-year earnings growth is beyond 2000 peaks.
After-tax corporate profits are nearly twice their 2000 share of GDP.

leverage.summary: Margin debt is at records and leveraged ETF assets doubled; margin loans relative to GDP score near the top of their history.

items.text: FINRA margin debt $1.4156 trillion in May, up 53.7% in a year; 6.17% of M2 against the 6.35% dot-com record.

fomo.summary: Record IPO issuance and a record household equity share both match the data.

items.text: SpaceX raised a record $75 billion in its IPO at about a $1.77 trillion valuation.
US IPO proceeds passed $110 billion by mid-June; Goldman forecasts a record $160 billion for 2026.

fragility.summary: Private-credit stress among small borrowers is rising, but public credit spreads are tight and financial conditions loose, so the data does not show it yet.

items.text: 12% of loans to $10-20 million EBITDA private-credit borrowers are priced below 90% of par, up from about 1% in 2023; record PIK use.

benchmark.summary: Concentration is a record and stocks barely out-yield bonds, but the Nasdaq is not unusually far ahead of the S&P 500.

items.text: The ten largest S&P 500 stocks are about 40% of the index, up from about 19% ten years earlier.
Alphabet fell 13% on 29 October, its worst day on record, while the equal-weighted S&P 500 rose 1.2%.

trend.summary: Real price is about 2.5 sigma above its long-run trend, past GMO's 2-sigma bubble line; only 1998-2000 stood further above it.

items.text: GMO defines a bubble as a 2-sigma move above trend; all 28 major bubbles in its 1997 study went back to trend.

killers.summary: The news is about tightening (a September Fed hike, CPI 3.7%, a 10-year yield near 5%); in the data only the bond-yield killer is on.

items.text: The Fed held at 3.75-4% on 28 October after a September hike; Cook and Hammack dissented for another hike.
September CPI rose 3.7% from a year earlier, above the 3.6% expected.
US chip stocks were set to lose about $2 trillion of value amid rate-hike bets and AI build-out costs.
